info.name: MnCardio — mobile API
info.description:
The endpoints the Android/iOS app needs, and nothing else.

See mobile/QUICKSTART.md to get started and mobile/API.md for the full contract.

How to use it:
1. Import mncardio.postman_environment.json and select it.
2. Fill patientUser / patientPassword / doctorUser / doctorPassword. Ask ITsystem for them — they are never committed.
3. Run `01 Auth → Patient login` and `01 Auth → Doctor login`. Each stores its token in the environment, and every other request picks it up automatically.

Two things to keep in mind while clicking around:

• The `/api/patient`, `/api/doctor` and `/api/auth` folders use the lowercase envelope `{success, message, data}` and real HTTP status codes.
• `/api/Chat`, `/api/Advice` and the login endpoints are the legacy layer: PascalCase `{Success, Message, Data, Option}`, POST for everything, and **HTTP 200 even on failure**. A green 200 in Postman does not mean the call worked — read the `Success` field.

The patient username is a Cyrillic registration number (ПП…), not Latin PP. Paste it, do not type it.

This collection is published to a public-facing repository. It must never contain a real credential.

item.name: 01 Auth
item.description: Login, session and password reset. Note the spelling split: the staff route is ForgetPassword, the patient route is ForgotPassword.

request.description:
Legacy envelope — the token is at **Data.token**, capital D. Stores it as {{patientToken}}.

The username is the patient's registration number and starts with Cyrillic letters (ПП…). A wrong password returns HTTP 200 with Success:false.
Excludes RoleId 4, and the account must have a linked DoctorsProfile row — without one, login fails even with the right password. Stores {{doctorToken}}.

item.name: Get a refresh token (Bearer access token)

request.description:
Neither login endpoint returns a refresh token. You trade a still-valid access token for one, once, by calling this with no body and the access token as Bearer.

Returns {token, refreshToken, expiresIn: 36000, LogedUser}. The refresh token lasts 30 days.

The steady-state refresh. Call it before the 10-hour access token expires rather than reacting to a 401.

An access token cannot be used as a refresh token or vice versa — refresh tokens carry typ:"refresh" and both are checked.

Says whether an access token is still good and who it belongs to, without provoking an error from a data endpoint. Use it on app launch.

Returns {Id, UserName, RoleId, OrganizationId, IsPatient}. Note RoleId is a **number** here and a **string** on /api/doctor/me.

Sends an emailed reset link. Public route. Spelled Forgot on the patient side and Forget on the staff side.

SMTP is not configured on the test server, so this will not actually deliver mail there.
Completes the reset. Token comes from the emailed link.
Requires a valid patient token. Changes the password of the account you are logged in as — on the test server this will change a shared test account, so coordinate before sending.
Note the spelling — ForgetPassword, not Forgot. Public route.

Password rule: at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character.

It is now defined once in helper/PasswordPolicy.js and enforced on both the staff and patient routes. The test server is still running an older build that accepts a weak patient password, so validate client-side regardless — see API.md § Passwords.
Returns success but invalidates nothing server-side — the token stays valid until it expires. Logging out is deleting your stored tokens.

item.name: 02 Patient — Үйлчлүүлэгчийн модуль
item.description:
Tender §2, modules 2.1–2.7. Lowercase envelope, real status codes, `?limit` (default 20, max 100) and `?offset`, `?from`/`?to` on the resource's own date column.

No endpoint here accepts a patient identifier — it always comes from the token. There is nowhere to put someone else's id, which is the point of the surface.

request.description: 404 NOT_FOUND if the account has no linked Patient row; 403 PATIENT_NOT_RESOLVED if the link is missing entirely.
Newest first. Returns blood_pressure and blood_pressure2 (diastolic).

`date` is required — omit it and you get 400 DATE_REQUIRED.

Asymmetry worth knowing: reads return blood_pressure2 but **create does not accept it**, so a patient cannot record diastolic pressure through this endpoint even though the chart plots it.

This writes to the shared test database.
Returns {labels, series:{blood_pressure, blood_pressure2, pulse, weight}} ascending, capped at 365 points. Built server-side so you just plot it.
`is_doctor` distinguishes the reply from the question. `doctor_name` is null on the patient's own entries.
`comment` required, else 400 COMMENT_REQUIRED. Writes to the shared test database.

Read-only by design — advice is doctor-authored.

Two data facts that change your UI: `body` is empty on 57% of tickets because the clinical content sits in the first reply (use `comments[0]`), and no notification is delivered when advice arrives. Do not build a badge you cannot feed.

Returns {bodySize, history} — raw inputs only. **No score and no risk class is computed**: the methodology and its risk classes are an unapproved ЗСҮТ deliverable.

Do not invent a formula. A wrong cardiovascular risk number shown to a patient is a clinical safety problem, not a rounding error.

Note two spellings in the payload: body weight is `bodySize.Weigth` (a typo baked into the database) and BMI comes back as `BJI`.

Fields are **PascalCase inside the lowercase envelope** — Id, Comment, CreateDate — because RemoteVisit is a newer-generation table. The envelope tells you nothing about the field names inside it.

This is a complaint box, not a booking system: no scheduling, no status, no doctor assignment, no video.
Capital C on `Comment` here, lowercase on /questions. Required, else 400 COMMENT_REQUIRED.

Returns 200 with an **empty array** on the test server today: the tables exist but no exercises have been seeded, because the exercise list, categories and the 39 videos are still customer decisions.

An empty list here is correct, not a broken endpoint. Unlike its siblings this route takes no limit/offset.
`ExerciseId` required, else 400 EXERCISE_REQUIRED. Since the exercise catalogue is empty today, any id you send is unmatched — expect this to be usable once exercises are seeded.
Returns {rows, labels, series:{pulse, spo2}}, capped at 365 points.
No validation at all on this one — every field is optional. Returns {Id}. Writes to the shared test database.
Latest assessment row, or null when there is none. `data: null` with success:true is the normal empty answer.

item.name: 03 Doctor — Эмчийн модуль
item.description:
Tender §2, tracker rows 28–32. Same conventions as the patient surface. No endpoint accepts a doctor, user or organisation identifier — all three come from the token.

Gate errors: 401 NOT_AUTHENTICATED, 403 NOT_A_DOCTOR (RoleId 4), 403 ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED (role outside 1/2/3/6), 403 ORGANIZATION_NOT_RESOLVED.

request.description:
Returns {UserId, DoctorId, RoleId, IsAdmin, FullName, profile, organization}.

**RoleId comes back as a string here** ("3") but as a number on /api/auth/session (3). Normalise it once at your client boundary.

`scope=mine` (default) is what this user recorded; `scope=organization` is the whole organisation including children. Admins see everything. `search` matches registration number, last name or first name.

Stores the first result's id as {{visitId}} for the next request.
Organisation-scoped: an id outside your scope returns **404, not the record**. That matters — Visit holds ~450,000 rows and an unscoped detail endpoint would be an enumeration hole.
Each row carries {id_data, since, patient, latestReading} — the most recent journal reading is included, so the screen needs no second call per patient.

The doctor is taken from the token; the body is ignored beyond PatientId.

Use this rather than the legacy /api/PatientMonitoring/SavePatient, which reads UserId and DoctorId from the request body and can therefore be pointed at another doctor's list.
Refuses a patient you do not monitor with 403 NOT_MONITORED.
Soft-removes from your own monitoring list. 404 if the patient is not on it. Writes to the shared test database.

filter = mine | drafts | all. The doctor's **own** tickets, each with a commentCount.

This is deliberately not the organisation-wide wall — that stays at /api/Advice/GetFeed with its own visibility rules.
Returns {ticket, comments}, author-scoped — someone else's ticket returns 404.

Counts for the phone summary: myVisits, organizationVisits, monitoredPatients, adviceAuthored, topDiagnoses.

`source` carries the organisation and timestamp provenance marking both tenders require on exports.
**Minimum 3 characters**, else 400 SEARCH_TOO_SHORT. Do not fire this on every keystroke — debounce it.
Returns {patient, visits[20], journal{labels, series}, isMonitoredByMe} — everything one screen needs in a single call.

item.name: 04 Chat — Телемедицин
item.description:
Legacy layer: POST for everything, PascalCase envelope, HTTP 200 on failure. Identity comes from the token — no route accepts a caller id.

Text, image, audio and documents are all supported, which covers the tender's chat requirement in full. Realtime fan-out is Socket.IO on /chatmessage; writes always go over HTTP.

request.description: Rooms with UnreadCount, LastMessage and Members. Stores the first room id as {{chatRoomId}}.
PageSize is capped at 50. Page with **BeforeId**, not page numbers — messages arrive while you scroll and offset paging would duplicate or skip them.

Text is capped at 2000 characters. `ClientMsgId` echoes back so you can reconcile an optimistic bubble.

With HasAttachment:true the message is created as pending and is **not** delivered until CommitMessage — see the attachment sequence below.

Sending an attachment is three calls, in order:

1. POST /api/Chat/SendMessage with HasAttachment:true → a pending message, delivered to nobody yet.
2. POST /api/BaseObject/uploadFile (multipart, LinkedObjectName 'ChatMessages', LinkedObjectId = the new MessageId).
3. POST /api/Chat/CommitMessage → promotes it to sent and fans it out over the socket.

Skip step 3 and the message never reaches anyone; if zero files landed the carrier message is deleted rather than left as an empty bubble.

Chat uploads get a 50 MB cap; everything else is 10 MB. Allowed extensions app-wide: jpg jpeg png gif webp bmp heic · pdf doc docx xls xlsx txt csv dcm · mp3 m4a aac ogg wav webm. **No video extension is on that list.**
Returns {Total, Rooms}. Poll this on app resume — a backgrounded phone receives nothing over the socket, because there is no FCM/APNs in the backend yet.
Idempotent — calling it twice returns the same room. UserType 'S' is staff, 'P' is patient.
Doctors only — patients can never be group members.

Rate-limited to 30 requests per minute — it is the national physician directory and the limit exists to stop it being bulk-scraped. Debounce your search box.

A patient's searches are scoped to their own care team.
Provinces and districts with counts, for the search filter UI.

Membership-checked, and the right route for chat files. The generic /api/BaseObject/downloadFile is also authorized (MayDownload, 403 on refusal) — an earlier note here claimed otherwise and was wrong — but prefer this one for chat.

Filter = all | open | closed | mine | drafts. Option carries {Total, PageNumber, PageSize, HasMore}.

Two data facts before you build filters: **no ticket has status 'n' (open)** — an open-only filter renders an empty screen — and `level` is NULL on 40% of rows, which makes those invisible to every non-admin.

`Search` needs at least 2 characters and matches the ticket body only.
Requires AdviceId — without it you get "Information is missing" at HTTP 200.
The full thread. On 57% of tickets the clinical content is here rather than in the ticket body.

The field names above are the ones the handler actually reads (all lowercase, and `cholestrol` is misspelled in the source). They are not the names the acceptance harness was sending, which is the likeliest reason it failed there.

Separately: the cardiovascular risk methodology and its risk classes are an unapproved customer deliverable. Even if this endpoint answers, do not surface a score in the app until ЗСҮТ has signed the methodology off.
